about: WATERS AND LANDMARKS TO FIND (Code/Game/Map/Discoveries.cs; the user, 9 Oct 2026: 'add waters to discover and land marks ect points of interest'). Each is a place on the chart that is not there until she has come within its reach: then it is found, the log says so, its dot stands on the chart (its name shows when the pointer rests on the dot), and Journey lists it. A thing found stays found. PLACEHOLDER TEXT: every 'note' is a draft for the user to overwrite, one or two plain sentences as a shipmaster would say them. NAMES: 'name' is what the chart says. Where a name of the time is known it is used, and 'then' says where it is written; where none is known the name is a plain one and 'then' is empty. 'today' is the place's name now, for whoever edits this file: the game never shows it. lat, lon: degrees. reach_km: how near she must come (left out: the kind's own). from, to: the years it is there (left out: always). Bake/world/check_discoveries.py checks every place against the sea lanes: nothing here lies where no ship can come.
credit: Places and coordinates: the project's own, from general geography. The names of the time are from the works named under 'then'.

things.name: The Rhine
things.today: Kromme Rijn, between Wijk bij Duurstede and Utrecht
things.then: Rhenus: the old course, the Rhine of the Romans and the Franks
things.note: The old river itself, past the quays of Dorestat to Traiectum and on to the dunes. Slow and winding, and every bend of it known.

things.name: The Lek
things.then: Lockia, in a charter of 777
things.note: The broad arm that leaves the Rhine at Dorestat and runs west. The quick way down to the Maas mouth and the sea.

things.name: The Vecht
things.then: Fectio in Roman times; Fehtna in the eighth century
things.note: North from Traiectum to the Almere. Narrow and slow, with reeds on both hands, and the short way to the Frisian markets.

things.name: The old mouth of the Rhine
things.then: ostium Rheni; the Roman fort at the mouth is the later Brittenburg
things.note: The Rhine of the Romans comes out here through the dunes, under the walls of a fort of theirs. It silts, and a laden boat waits for the tide over its bar.

things.name: The Kinnem shore
things.then: Kinnin or Kinnehem, a Frisian district in eighth century charters
things.note: A straight wall of dunes with no harbour in it for two days of rowing. Behind it lies fen, and nobody stands on the sand to ask the way of.

things.name: Wiron
things.then: Wiron, in the records of Fulda's lands, eighth century
things.note: A low island of clay and boulders where the Almere's marsh meets the sea. Frisian lords hold land on it.

things.name: The Almere
things.today: the south of the IJsselmeer and Flevoland
things.then: Aelmere, in Willibald's Life of Boniface, about 760
things.note: The inland sea of the Frisians. Shallow and brown, and wide enough to lose the land.

things.name: The Fli
things.then: Fli, in the Law of the Frisians, about 802
things.note: The gap in the islands where the Almere runs out to the sea. The Frisians' law changes at this water.

things.name: Texla
things.then: Texla, in records of the eighth and ninth centuries
things.note: The first of the sand islands. Its people take what the sea throws up, and ask no one.

things.name: The wads
things.note: Mud and sand behind the islands, dry at every ebb. A flat boat that knows the creeks goes from the Fli to the Laubach without meeting the open sea.

things.name: The Laubach
things.then: Laubachi, in the Law of the Frisians, about 802
things.note: A small river with a wide mouth. It parts the middle Frisians from the eastern ones, and the law is not the same on its two banks.

things.name: The mouth of the Ems
things.then: Amisia to the Romans; Emisa in the ninth century
things.note: A wide brown mouth between sands. Emuthon lies a tide's row inside it.

things.name: The mouth of the Wisura
things.then: Wisura, in the Royal Frankish Annals
things.note: The river of the Saxons. The Frisians' law ends on its west bank.

things.name: The mouth of the Albis
things.then: Albis, in the Royal Frankish Annals
things.note: The great river of the north. Beyond it the king's word is carried by armies, and not every year.

things.name: Fositesland
things.then: Fositesland, in Alcuin's Life of Willibrord, about 796
things.note: A red rock alone in the sea, holy to the god Fosite. No beast that grazes there is touched, and water is drawn from its spring in silence.

things.name: The Egidora
things.then: Egidora, in the Royal Frankish Annals
things.note: The Danes' border river. A boat goes far up it, and a short haul over land from its head reaches Sliesthorp and the eastern sea.

things.name: The outer lands
things.today: the North Frisian islands: Sylt, Föhr, Amrum
things.note: Low islands and marsh behind a broken line of dunes. Frisians have begun to settle them.

things.name: The Horn reef
things.note: A reef running far out to the west from Jutland's corner. Ships bound for Ripa stand well clear of it and then turn in.

things.name: The deeps off Ripa
things.note: Channels through the flats to the river of Ripa. They move from year to year, and the men of the place mark them with withies.

things.name: The Limfjord
things.then: Limafjord in later Norse writing
things.note: A sea gate through the north of Jutland, by sand bars that open and close. A ship that finds it open is spared the Skaw.

things.name: The Skaw
things.then: Skagi in later Norse writing
things.note: The last point of Jutland, a low spit of sand. Two seas meet off it and the water stands in a line.

things.name: The Jutland sea
things.note: The sea east of Jutland, with the Danes' islands at its foot. Shoal in the south and never far from a lee.

things.name: The Vik
things.then: Vik, the bay, in Norse writing
things.note: The great bay of the Northmen's south country. Skiringssal lies on its west side.

things.name: The Naze
things.then: Lidandisnes in later Norse writing
things.note: Norway's southern point. Round it the coast turns north and the sea changes.

things.name: The Jæren shore
things.then: Jadarr in later Norse writing
things.note: A long low shore with no harbour and a heavy surf. Ships pass it in one run and do not stop.

things.name: The Sound
things.then: Eyrarsund in later Norse writing
things.note: The narrow water between the Danes' great island and Skane. Most of what goes to the eastern sea goes through it.

things.name: The Belt
things.note: The wide passage between the Danes' islands. Strong streams, and a lee on one hand or the other in any wind.

things.name: The Slia
things.then: Slia, as in Sliesthorp, in the Royal Frankish Annals
things.note: A long narrow fjord running deep into Jutland's neck. Sliesthorp lies at its head.

things.name: The Danes' wall
things.then: The earliest timbers are of 737
things.note: An earth wall across the neck of Jutland, from the head of the Slia west to the marshes. The Danes' kings keep it up.

things.name: The white cape
things.note: White cliffs at the north end of the Rugians' island. The Wends are said to keep a god there.

things.name: Burgendaland
things.then: Burgenda land, in Wulfstan's voyage, about 890
things.note: A high island alone in the eastern sea. Its people have a king of their own.

things.name: Eowland
things.then: Eowland, in Wulfstan's voyage, about 890
things.note: A long narrow island lying along the Swedes' shore, flat as a board. A strait runs behind it.

things.name: Wislemutha
things.then: Wislemutha, in Wulfstan's voyage, about 890
things.note: The mouth of the Wisle. West of it is the Wends' land, east of it the Ests'.

things.name: The Estmere
things.then: Estmere, in Wulfstan's voyage, about 890
things.note: A lagoon behind a long spit of sand, fresh at one end and salt at the other. Truso stands on a lake beside it.

things.name: The Mälar
things.then: Logrinn, the Lake, in later Norse writing
things.note: A sea bay full of islands, reaching far into the Swedes' country. Birka is on one of them.

things.name: The Neva
things.note: A short strong river out of the great lake. Up it lies the road to the east and its silver.

things.name: The Maas mouth
things.today: the old estuary of the Maas, by Brielle and Hoek van Holland
things.then: Mosa, the river; Witla stood at its mouth
things.note: Where the Lek, the Waal and the Maas come down to the sea together. Witla lies just inside.

things.name: The Waal
things.then: Vahalis to the Romans
things.note: The southern arm of the Rhine, and the heavier water. The way up to Noviomagus.

things.name: The Isla
things.then: Isala; Hisla in the eighth century
things.note: The northern arm of the Rhine, to Daventre and the far shore of the Almere.

things.name: The parting of the waters
things.today: the old fork of Rhine and Waal, by Lobith
things.note: Where the river splits: one arm is the Waal, the other keeps the name of Rhine. Every shipman on the river knows the place.

things.name: The mouths of the Scald
things.then: Scaldis
things.note: The many mouths of the Scald among low islands. The banks here move between one summer and the next.

things.name: The Sincfal
things.then: Sincfal, in the Law of the Frisians, about 802
things.note: A tide creek on the Flemish shore. The Frisians' law reaches this far and no farther.

things.name: The Flemish banks
things.today: the banks off Ostend and Nieuwpoort
things.note: Long sands lying off a low shore, covered at half tide. The lead goes over the side here.

things.name: The narrows
things.note: Britain and Gaul in one look, white cliff on both hands. The tide runs hard through here and turns twice a day.

things.name: The light of Bononia
things.then: Bononia; the Royal Frankish Annals tell of the old light put in order in 811
things.note: A Roman tower on the cliff above Bononia, taller than anything on either shore. No fire has burned in it within memory, and shipmen steer by it all the same.

things.name: The old light at Dofras
things.today: the Roman pharos at Dover Castle
things.note: An eight-sided tower of the Romans on the cliff over Dofras, hollow and roofless. The white cliffs run away from it on both sides.

things.name: The long sands
things.note: A great bank off the Kentish shore, dry at low water and gone at high. Between it and the land is the best anchorage on the coast.

things.name: Reptacæstir
things.then: Reptacaestir, in Bede, 731
things.note: High flint walls of a Roman fort at the south mouth of the Wantsum. The legions landed here. Sheep graze inside it now.

things.name: The Wantsum
things.today: the Wantsum Channel, now dry land
things.then: Vantsumu, in Bede, 731
things.note: The channel that makes Tenet an island. Ships for Lundenwic go through it and not round the foreland.

things.name: Raculf
things.then: Raculf, in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle under 669
things.note: A minster built inside a Roman fort at the north mouth of the Wantsum. Its west front is the first thing seen of Kent from the Temes.

things.name: Tenet
things.then: Tanatos in Bede; Tenet in English
things.note: The island at Kent's corner, cut off by the Wantsum. Corn land, and a minster of the king's kinswomen.

things.name: Sceapig
things.then: Sceapige, in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle
things.note: Sheep island, at the mouth of the Medweg. A minster of nuns stands on its north cliff.

things.name: The Medweg
things.then: Medwaeg in English
things.note: The river of west Kent. A tide up it is Hrofescæster, with a bishop and a Roman bridge.

things.name: The mouth of the Temes
things.then: Temes in English; Tamesis in Latin
things.note: Wide, shallow and brown, with sands running out from both shores. The flood carries a ship to Lundenwic in two tides.

things.name: Ythancæstir
things.then: Ythancaestir, in Bede, 731
things.note: A stone church alone on the wall of a Roman fort at the edge of the marsh. Cedd built it. Ships take their bearing from it.

things.name: The fen bay
things.note: A broad shallow bay where the rivers of the fens come out. The banks dry for miles and the tide comes back faster than a man walks.

things.name: The Humbre
things.then: Humbre in English; Bede has it in Latin
things.note: The river that parts the Northumbrians from the southern English. Up it, and up the Use, lies Eoforwic.

things.name: The chalk head
things.note: A great white headland with sea birds in thousands on its ledges. The coast turns behind it.

things.name: Farne
things.then: Farne, in Bede, 731
things.note: Bare rock islands off Bebbanburg. Cuthbert lived alone on the nearest. The seals have it now.

things.name: Coludesburh
things.then: Coludi urbs, in Bede, 731
things.note: A high dark head with the stones of a burned monastery on it. Men and women lived there under one abbess, and the fire is said to have been a judgement.

things.name: The Forth
things.note: A long firth running west into the land. The English hold its south shore and the Picts its north.

things.name: The Picts' firth
things.then: Pettlandsfjord, the Picts' firth, in later Norse writing
things.note: Between the mainland and the Orcades. The tide here can stop a ship under full sail, or carry her through in an hour.

things.name: The Orcades
things.then: Orcades, in Bede and the old geographers
things.note: Green islands off the north of Britain, with tides like rivers between them.

things.name: The far islands
things.then: Hjaltland in later Norse writing
things.note: Treeless islands far out to the north, the last land before the open ocean.

things.name: The turning cape
things.then: Hvarf, the turning, in later Norse writing
things.note: The corner of Britain. Here a ship from the north turns south for the islands and Ireland.

things.name: Manau
things.then: Manau in Welsh; Manu in Irish
things.note: An island in the middle of the sea between Ireland and Britain. From its hill a man is said to see four kingdoms.

things.name: Môn
things.then: Mon in Welsh; Mona to the Romans
things.note: The corn island of the Britons, cut from the land by a strait that runs like a river.

things.name: Rechru
things.then: Rechru, in the Annals of Ulster
things.note: A small island off the Irish shore, with a church of Colum Cille's monks on it.

things.name: Étar
things.then: Benn Etair in Irish
things.note: A high rocky head closing the north side of the bay. Duiblinn lies behind it, up the river.

things.name: The Sæfern sea
things.then: Saefern in English; Sabrina in Latin
things.note: A long funnel of brown water between the Britons and the West Saxons. The tide here rises higher than anywhere known.

things.name: The land's end
things.note: The last rock of Britain to the south and west. The Britons of the west still hold it.

things.name: Vecta
things.then: Vecta, in Bede; Wiht in English
things.note: A chalk island closing the water before Hamwic. There are two ways in, and the tides in them do not agree.

things.name: The Soluente
things.then: Soluente, in Bede, 731
things.note: The water behind Vecta. The flood comes twice here, and a ship may lie afloat when all the coast is dry.

things.name: Selæseu
things.then: Selaeseu, the seal's island, in Bede, 731
things.note: A flat point with the South Saxons' bishop's church on it, and shoals all round.

things.name: The white head
things.note: The highest of the chalk cliffs. In clear air it is seen half a day's sail off.

things.name: The Limen
things.today: the old Rother estuary under Lympne
things.then: Limenaea in eighth century charters
things.note: A marsh river behind a bank of shingle. A fort of the Romans is sliding down the hill above it.

things.name: The bay of the Sumina
things.then: Sumina, in Gregory of Tours
things.note: A wide bay of sand that the sea leaves twice a day. Saint Valery's house stands on its south point.

things.name: The mouth of the Sequana
things.then: Sequana
things.note: The road to Rotomagus and Parisius. A wave comes up it with the spring tides and takes small boats that are not ready for it.

things.name: The cape of the Constantine shore
things.then: pagus Constantinus, the Cotentin
things.note: A stone finger pointing north, with islands beyond it. The stream between runs faster than a boat can be rowed.

things.name: Saint Michael's at Tumba
things.then: Mons Tumba; the church is of 708
things.note: A rock in a bay of quicksand with the archangel's church on its top. The sea comes round it faster than a horse.

things.name: Uxantis
things.then: Uxantis, in the Roman road books
things.note: The last island of Gaul, in a sea of rocks and fog. Ships for the Loire turn south here.

things.name: The mouth of the Garumna
things.then: Garumna
things.note: A wide brown mouth with a bar across it and a tide like a mill race. Burdigala is two tides up.

things.name: The bar of the Quantia
things.today: the bar of the Canche below Quentovic
things.then: Quentovic is the wic on the Quantia (the Canche)
things.note: The river of Quentovic comes out over a bar of sand. With the wind in the west there is white water on it, and a boat waits for the flood.

things.name: The race off the long bill
things.note: Off the long stone point the tide boils even on a still day. A boat goes far outside it, or hard under the rock.

things.name: The race of Sena
things.then: Pomponius Mela (c. 43): the island Sena
things.note: Between the last point of the land and the island of Sena the tide runs like a river in spate. It is passed at slack water or not at all.

things.name: The south roost
things.today: Sumburgh Roost, off the south head of Shetland
things.note: Off the south head of the far islands two tides meet and stand up against each other. In a wind against it no boat lives there.

things.name: Brecan's cauldron
things.then: Adomnan, Life of Columba (c. 700): Charybdis Brecani
things.note: Between two islands the flood turns round on itself and roars. They say a king's son went down in it with fifty ships.

things.name: The race off Cenn Tire
things.today: the race off the Mull of Kintyre
things.then: Annals of Ulster: Cenn Tire
things.note: Where the narrow sea between the two lands is narrowest, the tide runs hard round the head and the sea is never quiet there.

things.name: The Stad
things.today: Stad, the west cape of Norway
things.note: A blunt high cape with no islands to hide behind. Boats wait days for a morning quiet enough to round it, and some drag over the neck of land instead.

when_the_rivers_are_built.name: The great lake
when_the_rivers_are_built.note: Fresh water with no far shore in sight, and a sea's weather on it. Aldeigjuborg lies up a river at its south end.

when_the_rivers_are_built.name: Sanctos
when_the_rivers_are_built.note: A church over the graves of the soldier martyrs. Beside it stand the walls of a dead Roman city, quarried for their stone.

when_the_rivers_are_built.name: Suitbert's island
when_the_rivers_are_built.note: An island in the river, given to the English bishop Suitbert a hundred years ago. His monks are there still.

when_the_rivers_are_built.name: The seven hills
when_the_rivers_are_built.note: Where the hills close in on the river above Bonna. From here up the Rhine runs in a gorge.

when_the_rivers_are_built.name: Confluentes
when_the_rivers_are_built.note: Where the Mosella comes in. An old Roman wall stands at the meeting, and a house of the king inside it.

when_the_rivers_are_built.name: The narrow water
when_the_rivers_are_built.today: the Rhine gorge at the Loreley
when_the_rivers_are_built.note: The river squeezed between rock walls, fast and deep, with a reef under the east cliff. Boats are hauled up it on ropes.

when_the_rivers_are_built.name: The reef at Bingium
when_the_rivers_are_built.note: A bar of rock across the river. Cargo goes round it by cart, or the boat is dragged through on a rope.

_when_the_rivers_are_built: NOT READ BY THE GAME. The Rhine above the delta, and the Neva up to the great lake, have no lanes a ship can use yet (they are baked as rivers still to be built), so these seven could never be found. Move them up into things when Colonia, Mogontia and Aldeigjuborg can be reached.
